name: ACL Reconstruction Rehabilitation
summary: ACL reconstruction replaces the torn ligament with a graft (commonly hamstring tendons, patellar tendon, or quadriceps tendon). The graft goes through a period of weakening and remodelling ("ligamentisation") over many months, so rehabilitation and return to sport must respect biology and meet functional criteria.

looksLike: Goals before surgery: no swelling, full extension, good quadriceps activation, normal gait.
Patients who enter surgery with good range and strength tend to recover better.
redFlags: Fever, red hot wound, increasing swelling
Loss of extension that does not improve (block)
New giving way, large effusion after a pivot
firstSteps: 1: Early (about 0 to 2 weeks): Swelling control, full extension, quadriceps activation (quads sets, SLR), walking with crutches as needed; Full extension, SLR without lag, minimal effusion, normal gait
2: Strength (about 2 to 12 weeks): Closed and open chain strengthening, balance, cycling; Effusion trace or less, full range, good single-leg control

measures: Effusion, range, quadriceps LSI, hop LSI, IKDC, ACL-RSI.

rows: Swelling control, full extension, quadriceps activation (quads sets, SLR), walking with crutches as needed
Full extension, SLR without lag, minimal effusion, normal gait
Closed and open chain strengthening, balance, cycling
Effusion trace or less, full range, good single-leg control
Quadriceps LSI around 70 to 80%, pain-free hop in place [Ref – to verify]
Strength LSI near 90%, good hop symmetry, movement quality
Meets battery of criteria; usually not before about 9 months for pivoting sport [Ref – to verify]

blocks.text: Open chain knee extension can begin early within a limited range (often 90 to 45 degrees), progressing range over time, as per protocol [Ref – to verify].

rows: Quadriceps sets, SLR, heel props for extension
Leg press, squats, step-ups, split squats
3 to 4 sets of 6 to 12, progress load
Hamstring curls (delay or adapt with hamstring graft)

blocks.text: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation for quadriceps activation early [Ref – to verify]; cryotherapy and compression for swelling.

items: **Why is full extension a priority in week 1?** Loss of extension causes abnormal gait and long-term problems.
**What is LSI?** Limb symmetry index: involved limb as a percentage of the uninvolved limb.
**Why use criteria and not time alone?** Patients progress at different rates; criteria reduce reinjury risk.
**How does a meniscal repair change the protocol?** Often restricted weight-bearing and deep flexion for weeks.
**Why measure psychological readiness?** Fear and low confidence affect return to sport and reinjury risk.
